result.topic_en: Euler tabulates, by induction, for which forms of prime divisors the numbers ±1, ±2, ±3, ±5, ±6, ±7, ±10, ±11, ±12, ±14, ±15 are quadratic residues, and begins observations toward a demonstration, with marginal notes.
result.transcription:
42 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
342. Numerus $+4$ semper ad residua refertur, et de $-4$ idem est judicium ac de $-1$. Numerus autem 5 reperitur inter residua, si divisor sit vel $20q+1$, vel $20q+9$, vel $20q+11$, vel $20q+19$; at $-5$ inter residua deprehenditur, si divisor sit vel $20q+1$, vel $20q+3$, vel $20q+7$, vel $20q+9$.
343. Colligamus haec, ut uni conspectui exponantur:
Inter residua erit numerus | si divisor primus fuerit
$+1$ | $4q+(1, 3)$
$-1$ | $4q+1$
$+2$ | $8q+(1, 7)$ (*)
$-2$ | $8q+(1, 3)$
$+3$ | $12q+(1, 11)$
$-3$ | $12q+(1, 7)$
$+5$ | $20q+(1, 9, 11, 19)$
$-5$ | $20q+(1, 3, 7, 9)$
$+6$ | $24q+(1, 5, 19, 23)$
$-6$ | $24q+(1, 5, 7, 11)$
$+7$ | $28q+(1, 3, 9, 19, 25, 27)$
$-7$ | $28q+(1, 9, 11, 15, 23, 25)$
$+10$ | $40q+(1, 3, 9, 13, 27, 31, 37, 39)$
$-10$ | $40q+(1, 7, 9, 11, 13, 19, 23, 37)$
$+11$ | $44q+(1, 9, 25, 5, 7, 37, 39, 19, 35, 43)$
$-11$ | $44q+(1, 9, 25, 5, 37, 3, 15, 23, 27, 31)$
$+12$ | $48q+(1, 11, 13, 23, 25, 35, 37, 47)$
$-12$ | $48q+(1, 13, 25, 37, 7, 19, 31, 43)$
$+14$ | $56q+(1, 5, 9, 13, 25, 45, 11, 31, 43, 47, 51, 55)$
$-14$ | $56q+(1, 5, 9, 13, 25, 45, 3, 15, 19, 23, 27, 39)$
$+15$ | $60q+(1, 7, 11, 17, 43, 49, 53, 59)$
$-15$ | $60q+(1, 17, 49, 53, 19, 23, 31, 47)$ (**)
etc.
344. Haec autem hactenus tantum inductione nituntur, atque ad demonstrationem investigandam juvabit sequentia observasse. Primo, numerus quicunque $\pm n$ inter residua reperietur, si divisor primus fuerit formae $4nq+1$, vel adeo $4nq+ii$, denotante $i$ numerum imparem quemcunque.
Scripturae ad marginem;
(*) $xx-2yy$ alios divisores primos non admittit, nisi formae $8q+(1,7)$.
(**) 1) Si $xx=mn+r$, tum quadratum $xx$ tam per $m$ quam $n$ divisum, idem relinquet residuum $r$. Ergo si residuum $r$ convenit divisori $m$, conveniet etiam divisori $n$.
2) Si | divisor | inter non-resid. | residuum
| $4n-1$ | $-1$ |
| $8n-1$ | $-2$ | $+2$
| $8n-3$ | $\pm 2$ |
| $12n-1$ | $-3$ | $+3$
| $12n-7$ | $\pm 3$ |
| $8n\pm 3$ | $+2$ |
Hoc demonstrari potest; at si divisor $8n+1$, inter residua est $+2$, quod autem hinc non demonstratur.

methods.what: 4 is always a quadratic residue; -4 behaves like -1
methods.quote: Numerus $+4$ semper ad residua refertur, et de $-4$ idem est judicium ac de $-1$.

methods.what: Prime moduli for which 5 and -5 are quadratic residues
methods.quote: Numerus autem 5 reperitur inter residua, si divisor sit vel $20q+1$, vel $20q+9$, vel $20q+11$, vel $20q+19$; at $-5$ inter residua deprehenditur, si divisor sit vel $20q+1$, vel $20q+3$, vel $20q+7$, vel $20q+9$.

methods.what: Table of residue classes of primes p for which ±n (n up to 15) is a quadratic residue mod p
methods.quote: Inter residua erit numerus | si divisor primus fuerit

methods.what: ±n is a quadratic residue of primes of form 4nq+1 or 4nq+i^2, i odd
methods.quote: numerus quicunque $\pm n$ inter residua reperietur, si divisor primus fuerit formae $4nq+1$, vel adeo $4nq+ii$, denotante $i$ numerum imparem quemcunque.

methods.what: Prime divisors of x^2-2y^2 are of form 8q±1
methods.quote: $xx-2yy$ alios divisores primos non admittit, nisi formae $8q+(1,7)$.

methods.what: If x^2=mn+r, x^2 leaves residue r mod both m and n, so a residue of m transfers to n
methods.quote: Si $xx=mn+r$, tum quadratum $xx$ tam per $m$ quam $n$ divisum, idem relinquet residuum $r$.

items.quote: Haec autem hactenus tantum inductione nituntur, atque ad demonstrationem investigandam juvabit sequentia observasse.
items.english: These results so far rest only on induction, and to seek a demonstration it will help to have observed the following.

items.quote: Primo, numerus quicunque $\pm n$ inter residua reperietur, si divisor primus fuerit formae $4nq+1$, vel adeo $4nq+ii$, denotante $i$ numerum imparem quemcunque.
items.english: First, any number ±n will be found among the residues if the prime divisor is of the form 4nq+1, or even 4nq+i², where i denotes any odd number.

items.quote: $xx-2yy$ alios divisores primos non admittit, nisi formae $8q+(1,7)$.
items.english: x²−2y² admits no prime divisors other than those of the form 8q+(1,7).

items.quote: Hoc demonstrari potest; at si divisor $8n+1$, inter residua est $+2$, quod autem hinc non demonstratur.
items.english: This can be demonstrated; but if the divisor is 8n+1, +2 is among the residues, which however is not demonstrated from this.
